what: The public-domain texts Tolkien worked FROM. Not the corpus, and not tiered.
why_not_corpus: corpus/ is the population a claim about Arda may be cited to; these make no claim about Arda. They are evidence about Tolkien and about the tradition he wrote inside. See map/gen_analogues.py.
why_not_tiered: the tiers rank claims about Arda. These make none, so they carry a hand and a provenance instead, as fonts and map data do under section 8 ruling 3. There is no fifth tier.

analogues.title: Beowulf
analogues.hand: anonymous, c. 8th-11th century; this edition ed. James A. Harrison & Robert Sharp
analogues.why_here: Held because this archive already holds Tolkien's lecture 'Beowulf: The Monsters and the Critics', and a reader of the lecture had no way to reach the poem it is about.

analogues.title: Kalevala, volume I
analogues.language: Finnish, in W. F. Kirby's English verse translation
analogues.hand: compiled Elias Lönnrot; trans. W. F. Kirby
analogues.why_here: Tolkien wrote a 'Story of Kullervo', which this archive does NOT hold; this is the Kalevala that story is drawn from. Whether and how it shaped Turin is a claim this register does not make. VOLUME I ONLY.

analogues.title: Pearl
analogues.language: Middle English, in Sophie Jewett's verse translation
analogues.hand: anonymous, late 14th century (the Gawain-poet); trans. Sophie Jewett
analogues.why_here: Tolkien published a translation of Pearl in 1975. THIS IS JEWETT'S TRANSLATION, not his and not the Middle English -- recorded so nobody quotes it as either.

analogues.title: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
analogues.hand: anonymous, late 14th century; this edition ed. Richard Morris (EETS)
analogues.why_here: Tolkien and E. V. Gordon published an edition of this poem in 1925 -- bibliography, not interpretation. This is the Middle English, thorns and yoghs intact, and NOT their edition, which the archive does not hold.

analogues.title: The Volsunga Saga
analogues.language: Old Norse, in William Morris & Eirikr Magnusson's prose
analogues.why_here: The Sigurd matter. Tolkien's own 'Legend of Sigurd and Gudrun' is a DECLARED ABSENCE in this archive, so the source is held while the retelling is not.
